context: In this paper, we have given a framework to design exponential-time approximation schemes for basic graph partitioning problems. Our work points to several interesting directions for follow-up work. 1. A natural set of questions in this direction is that of obtaining exact algorithms faster than 2n nO(1) for Steiner k-cut and Multicut. For k-way cut, such an algorithm has been recently obtained [23]. In fact, the same question is open for 2-CSP, also Min 2-SAT. 2. Note that our techniques lead to randomized algorithms. Obtaining deterministic versions of our algorithms is an interesting question. 3. Could one design an appropriate “solution linearization” procedure for Multicut when the number of requests is unbounded? If the number of requests is constant, then Lemma 19 can be used to obtain such a procedure. 4. Our techniques (e.g., random contraction) break down for directed graphs. Could one build a similar framework that can handle directed problems?
